_comment: Setup-parameter registry, one entry per tunable: identity, value space, direction semantics, typical window, change effort, mechanism, optional phase affinity, notes, recommendation_target. Entries with a car_data.json lookup cite the section in 'notes'; direction_semantics checked against the digitised values. value_source: 'setup_sheet' (maps_to = car.json path) or 'logged_data' (maps_to null, truth is a logged channel) -- independent of recommendation_target.

arb_fl.label: Front-Left ARB Position

typical_window.notes: 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused; rear usually a slightly lower position than front

arb_fl.mechanism: Sets front-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets front lateral-load-transfer share, which sets front grip share relative to rear.
arb_fl.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.front (6.3..20.6 N/mm at drop link, ratio_to_wheel 1.07) -- verified: position 1->6.3 N/mm, position 7->20.6 N/mm, monotonic increasing, confirms 1=softest. Position-to-stiffness convention (linear vs squared) unresolved -- flagged convention_unresolved, unresolved. Four fully independent per-corner targets, no pairing concept.

arb_fr.label: Front-Right ARB Position

typical_window.notes: 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused; rear usually a slightly lower position than front

arb_fr.mechanism: Sets front-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets front lateral-load-transfer share, which sets front grip share relative to rear.
arb_fr.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.front. Four fully independent per-corner targets, no pairing concept.

arb_rl.label: Rear-Left ARB Position

typical_window.notes: usually a slightly lower position than front; 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused

arb_rl.mechanism: Sets rear-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets rear lateral-load-transfer share, which sets rear grip share relative to front.
arb_rl.notes: Stiffness lookup: car_data.json arb.rear (26.9..80.1 N/mm at drop link, ratio_to_wheel 0.77) -- verified: position 1->26.9 N/mm, position 7->80.1 N/mm, monotonic increasing, confirms 1=softest. Same convention_unresolved flag as front.

arb_rr.label: Rear-Right ARB Position

typical_window.notes: usually a slightly lower position than front; 2/6 rare, 1/7 unused

arb_rr.mechanism: Sets rear-axle roll-stiffness share, which sets rear lateral-load-transfer share, which sets rear grip share relative to front.

arb_front_mount.label: Front ARB Mount

typical_window.notes: Full legal enum is the window -- no numeric quantity underlies this parameter (setup_windows.json parameter_windows.arb_front_mount), so no narrower nominal + span; option set only.

arb_front_mount.mechanism: Upright mount couples steering input to ARB preload -- higher position gives a more direct/snappy turn-in response.
arb_front_mount.notes: No source image digitises this parameter -- mechanism from team knowledge only, no car_data.json cross-check. Stored in car.json's 'car' dict alongside differential_position / wing_position / splitter_offset.

springs_front.label: Front Springs
springs_front.mechanism: Sets front-axle vertical (ride) stiffness independent of roll stiffness; conditions which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) is valid.
springs_front.notes: Damper matrix conditions the recommended damper windows on the installed spring pairing -- see dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing, cells keyed '{front}x{rear}'.

springs_rear.label: Rear Springs
springs_rear.mechanism: Sets rear-axle vertical (ride) stiffness independent of roll stiffness; conditions which damper window (car_data.json dampers.matrix_by_spring_pairing) is valid.

ride_height_front.label: Front Ride Height

typical_window.notes: Floor only: standard - 2 mm (diffuser floor limit). No upper limit -- often run at the minimum, not required (author ruling); setup_state reads this as lower bound only.

ride_height_front.adjustment_step_derived_from: 1 mm per recommended change, author ruling 2026-10-23 (4f item 1, ride heights become M4 levers)
ride_height_front.mechanism: Sets front floor/splitter proximity to the ground -- aero platform height; FIA and aero conventions quoted at a constant offset, aero wears so the measured value is used to verify, not independently settable.
ride_height_front.notes: Convention offsets: car_data.json ride_height_measuring_points (FIA/ADAC/Porsche-laser, per corner X/Y/Z). Not itself a free target -- both readings move together.

ride_height_rear.label: Rear Ride Height
ride_height_rear.adjustment_step_derived_from: 1 mm per recommended change, author ruling 2026-10-23 (4f item 1, ride heights become M4 levers)
ride_height_rear.mechanism: Sets rear floor/diffuser exit height -- aero platform height and rake (with ride_height_front); FIA and aero conventions quoted at a constant offset.

diff_package.label: Differential Package
diff_package.mechanism: Selects the spring/ramp preload package that determines the diff's locking-torque-vs-position curve (see diff_position).
diff_package.notes: Reference curve: car_data.json diff_locking_torque (installed_package '8304N_1372N_30-5'). ~2h to change; context only, not a session-level target.

diff_position.label: Differential Position

typical_window.notes: full 5 sheet positions are the window, no narrower team-typical sub-range recorded

diff_position.mechanism: Sets clutch-pack preload/locking torque on the installed diff package -- more locking torque resists axle-speed difference under power, affecting exit rotation vs. traction.
diff_position.notes: Locking torque lookup: car_data.json diff_locking_torque.positions (30-5 package: 1 -> 70 Nm .. 5 -> 250 Nm, monotonic increasing) -- confirms 1 = least. Locking torque per position drifts with wear (measured continuously by the team; car.json would need a per-position torque field). Coupled to engine braking: teams run high diff and per-corner EB weakens it in-corner; the EB program is unknown in the data, which limits diff recommendations. Unit 'position' (the 5 sheet positions).

wing_position.label: Wing Position

typical_window.notes: Full legal enum is the window: a numeric anchor exists (angles_deg) but Outing.setup_data stores the enum label, not the angle (setup_windows.json parameter_windows.wing_position), so a numeric nominal + span would compare against the wrong representation.

wing_position.mechanism: Rear wing angle sets rear downforce -- affects high-speed balance (more angle = more rear grip/stability, less top speed).
wing_position.notes: Legal set confirmed against car_data.json wing_position_table's 'GT3 R 2026' column: only 7.3/8.3/9.3 deg (P8/P9/P10) have an entry.

toe_front.label: Front Toe
toe_front.mechanism: Front toe-out sharpens initial turn-in response at the cost of straight-line stability and tyre wear.
toe_front.notes: No digitised car_data table backs this parameter's direction (the toe-vs-wheel-travel kinematic curves were pruned as no-consumer) -- value space/direction from team knowledge only.

toe_rear.label: Rear Toe
toe_rear.mechanism: Rear toe-in adds straight-line and corner-exit stability at the cost of some rear tyre wear.
toe_rear.notes: Team knowledge only, no car_data table backing (same as toe_front).

camber_fl.label: FL Camber
camber_fl.adjustment_step_derived_from: team practice per this entry's notes: a camber change is two 0.1 deg clicks (0.2 deg); author ruling 2026-10-23 (4f item 7)
camber_fl.mechanism: Sets static camber -- dictated by tyre usage/temperature distribution across the contact patch.
camber_fl.notes: Base -3.5 deg front. Team knowledge only, no car_data table backing (camber-vs-wheel-travel curves pruned, no consumer). One click = 0.1 deg; a typical change is two clicks, 0.2 deg (adjustment_step; project-lead review). A tyre-surface / wear-pattern inspection precedes any camber change; a single-corner change is sometimes preferred over the symmetric pair. change_effort half_hour (20-30 min).

tc_lat.label: Traction Control - Lateral

value_space.feasible_derived_from: manufacturer TC table monotonic only from 2 to 11 (0 / 1 not on the same scale, see direction_semantics and notes); a decrease from 2 is at limit. Author ruling 2026-10-23 (4f item 3)

direction_semantics.1: driver modulation, minimal TC support (wording near-identical to 0; the scale is not cleanly monotonic between 0/1 and 2 -- see notes)
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted car rotation under lateral load on power = MORE TC intervention/support

typical_window.notes: window is 1..11, NON-LINEAR (per-position semantics from TC_reference table, not raw arithmetic) -- 0 (off) excluded from the tuning window, it is a distinct state, not the window floor. 5 = 'normal conditions' per source table; increase toward 11 for more support, decrease toward 2 for more permitted rotation.

tc_lat.mechanism: Sets how much car rotation the TC system permits during the lateral-loaded cornering phase (power applied while cornering); higher position = less permitted rotation = more intervention.
tc_lat.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel (feel, tyre life, fuel load); the current value is a logged quantity, not a setup-sheet value, and stays not assessable (channels.json ecu_B_tc_act: LAT / LON position mapping undocumented). Direction verified against car_data.json tc (TC_reference.png, current LAT/LON system): 2 'even more rotation', 3 'increased rotation', 4 'slightly more rotation', 5 'normal conditions', 6 'less rotation', 8-9 'increased TC support', 10 'strongly increased TC support', 11 'lots of TC support' -- monotonically less rotation permitted from 2 to 11, the opposite of a naive 'higher = more rotation' reading. Position 1 reads near-identical to 0 (low intervention next to the floor, not continuing the 2-11 trend) -- flagged, not smoothed. Supersedes the 2023-25 single-switch TC_1.png system (not digitised).

tc_lon.label: Traction Control - Longitudinal

value_space.feasible_derived_from: manufacturer TC table monotonic only from 2 to 11 (0 / 1 not on the same scale, see direction_semantics and notes); a decrease from 2 is at limit. Author ruling 2026-10-23 (4f item 3)

direction_semantics.0: driver modulation, little TC support -- NOTE: per project docs, TC LON at 0 does NOT disable TC (only TC LAT=0 does); wording matches position 1
direction_semantics.increasing_2_to_11: LESS permitted wheel spin under longitudinal load = MORE TC intervention/support

typical_window.notes: window is 1..11, NON-LINEAR (per-position semantics from TC_reference table, not raw arithmetic) -- 0 excluded from the tuning window (does NOT disable TC for tc_lon, see direction_semantics, but is still not part of the intervention-severity scale). 5 = 'normal conditions' per source table.

tc_lon.mechanism: Sets how much wheel spin the TC system permits during high-torque longitudinal phases (1st/2nd gear power-down on exit); higher position = less permitted spin = more intervention, useful for managing rear-tyre degradation.
tc_lon.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel; current value not assessable (see tc_lat). Direction verified against car_data.json tc: monotonically less wheel spin permitted from 2 to 11, 5 = baseline. TC LON = 0 does not switch TC off (TC_1.png introductory text, still true for the current system; only TC LAT has an off state).

abs_position.label: ABS Position

direction_semantics.type: categorical, NOT a single monotonic soft/hard axis
direction_semantics.1_to_8: dry maps -- 1-4 grouped 'High' overall grip level (1=baseline dry-high, 2/4=more stable FA/RA variants, 3=printed 'BL Medium grip map' despite its own row being categorised 'High' -- verified as printed, not a transcription error), 5-8 grouped 'Medium' overall grip level (5=baseline medium, 6=more stable, 7-8=add lateral support)
direction_semantics.9_to_11: wet maps ascending severity -- 9=baseline good-wet-grip, 10=rain tyres/heavy wet (limited deceleration), 11=monsoon emergency (highly limited deceleration)

typical_window.type: categorical brackets, not a numeric min/max distance (see direction_semantics.type)
typical_window.notes: Per ABS_2 V2 table (car_data.json abs, installed_config V2): sweet-spot search stays WITHIN the bracket appropriate to conditions; jumping across brackets (e.g. 4 to 9) is not a valid tuning move.

abs_position.mechanism: Selects the ABS intervention map; team practice is a sweet-spot search within the dry or wet bracket appropriate to conditions, not a linear soft-to-hard sweep.
abs_position.notes: Driver-adjustable mid-session from the steering wheel; current value from logged data, not the setup sheet. Trusted channel log_abs_pos (dash / steering-wheel domain; agrees with log_rt_abs_pos and stw_rt04_abs, while the ECU-domain abs_switch_pos disagrees on GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt; author decision, channels.json). Installed config V2 (ABS_2.png header 'Map for ABS configuration option "V2"'); full table car_data.json abs; Monza2 / CTMP / V4 not installed, not digitised. Categorical, not one monotonic axis: jumping across grip-level brackets (e.g. 4 to 9) is not a tuning move; within one bracket an ordinal +1 / +2 step is used in practice as a stability nudge toward the front- or rear-axle-stable variant (project-lead review).

brake_bias.label: Brake Bias

value_space.note: direction convention (fwd vs rear) and the channel's own identity are still open -- not invented here

brake_bias.mechanism: Driver-exclusive in-corner adjustment; braking-phase target only. Not evaluable for current-state window until the bias channel is identified [E].
brake_bias.notes: Recommendation target. Lockup chain behind it (Segers C5-1/2, docs/segers_bridge_review.md). The value comes from logged data, not the setup sheet; the brake-bias channel is not identified, so direction_semantics stays null and typical_window not assessable rather than invented.

splitter_offset.label: Splitter Offset

direction_semantics.hard_limit: the NEGATIVE extreme (more front downforce) is bounded by front-splitter/track contact, track-dependent -- HARD edge. The positive extreme is a range limit only, no physical contact -- SOFT edge. Author-elicited 2026-09-22 (Phase C), resolving Phase A's own unresolved placeholder ('sign convention unresolved, not invented, flagged for elicitation') -- see thesis_notes.md for the full provenance record.

typical_window.notes: full legal range is the window; hard forward limit (negative extreme only) is track-dependent, not a fixed sub-range

splitter_offset.mechanism: Front aero balance trim -- high-speed balance lever, paired to wing_position (same aero axis) and ride_height_front (shared ground clearance).
splitter_offset.notes: change_effort minutes (2 min sloppy / 20 min precise, author-elicited). No car_data digitisation of the offset-to-effect relationship. Direction convention (author-elicited): negative = more front downforce, positive = less; not symmetric -- negative approaches a hard physical edge (splitter/track contact), positive only a range limit. Known simplification: setup_state._window_edge_check treats both value_space ends as hard.

kinematic_variants.label: Kinematic Variants
kinematic_variants.mechanism: Homologated suspension-geometry variants (front FS-series, rear RS-series); background context for interpreting damper ratio / roll centre / antidive-antisquat behaviour, not a session-level tunable.
